+# Postmortem: High P99 Latency & Flapping Request Jitter on booklogr-api
+
+## Summary
+The `booklogr-api` service experienced high p99 latency (>2.4s) and request jitter on the `/v1/books/search` endpoint, triggering `BooklogrApiLatencyP99High` and `EdgeClientRequestJitter` alerts.
+
+## Root Cause
+1. **Search Cache Key Omission**: In `api/routes/books.py`, `@cache.cached` key_prefix used `request.path` instead of `request.full_path`, causing all search requests for a user to collide on the same cache key ignoring `?q=`.
+2. **Unreachable External Provider & Timeout Blocking**: In `api/config.py` and `api/book_provider.py`, data providers defaulted to external endpoints (`openlibrary` and `https://metadata.booklogr.app`) with 30s timeouts. When cache misses occurred, external calls timed out, blocking Gunicorn worker processes and causing severe request latency jitter.
+
+## Evidence Used
+- **Alertmanager / Prometheus Signals**: Alertmanager alerted on `BooklogrApiLatencyP99High` (p99 latency 2.485s). Prometheus metric `flask_http_request_duration_seconds` confirmed `/v1/books/search` as the slow route.
+- **Git Log**: Commit `8c580a7` introduced `key_prefix=lambda: f"view/{get_current_user_id()}/{request.path}"`.
+- **Network Probing**: Verified `https://openlibrary.org` timed out while local service `http://book-metadata:8080` responded in <5ms.
+
+## Changes Made
+1. **`api/routes/books.py`**: Updated `@cache.cached` key_prefix lambda to use `request.full_path` so query parameters (`?q=...`) produce unique cache keys.
+2. **`api/config.py`**: Changed default `DATA_PROVIDER` and `DATA_PROVIDER_FALLBACK` to local endpoint `http://book-metadata:8080`.
+3. **`api/book_provider.py`**: Updated default fallback URL to `http://book-metadata:8080` and reduced request timeouts from 30s to 5s.
